study.sampling_method: Curated high-quality Amazon Mechanical Turk adult sample collected in October 2024.

sample_flow.note: Participants were randomized across seven events and three framing conditions.
Respondents failing at least two of three instruction-comprehension checks were excluded as preregistered.

study.representativeness_note: The source describes a curated MTurk sample, not a probability-based nationally representative sample.

design_structure.description: Seven selected real-world news events spanning multiple topics.
Positive, neutral, and negative article conditions; each participant was assigned to one event and one frame.

study.preregistration_note: The article reports preregistration at AsPredicted.org (5mzn-n7dj) and states that the comprehension-check exclusion rule was preregistered.

model_match: The current CBD uses the negative-versus-neutral direction and nested-null contrast as validation targets. Published magnitudes are context only and are not used to set the appraisal gain.
limitations: The experiment varies sentence selection by tone and therefore combines information-selection and tone variation. The M1 scalar variables and bounded linear appraisal update are model constructs, not measured states from the study. The participant pool was a curated Amazon Mechanical Turk sample, so population representativeness should not be inferred.

study.sampling_method: Netquest online panels stratified by age, education, gender, and region against current census data in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Colombia.
study.representativeness_note: The source reports stratification to census demographics and robustness weights for minor education/gender deviations; the sample comes from online panels rather than a simple probability sample.

design_structure.description: Separate survey experiments in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, and Colombia.
Confirmation and refutation frames are the primary randomized contrast; additional brand/label or placebo variants differ by country.

study.preregistration_note: The article states that its hypotheses were preregistered on the Open Science Framework before data collection.

model_match: The current CBD uses the cross-country confirmation-greater-than-refutation engagement direction as the target for the frame-only candidate. The published percentage-point effects are context only and do not set beta_frame.
limitations: Aggregate engagement combines like, share and comment. Share alone is statistically significant only in Argentina, so the target validates active-engagement intent rather than the retained M0 Share process. The four-country samples were recruited from Netquest online panels with demographic stratification and robustness weighting; this supports balanced experimental contrasts but should not be read as unrestricted population representativeness.

study.sampling_method: Netquest Behavior Panel of Argentine adults using non-interlocking quotas on age, sex, and province calibrated to the adult population.

sample_flow.note: Base used for descriptive population-benchmark comparisons.
Regression base after excluding missing treatment assignment or model covariates.

study.representativeness_note: The paper describes the design as nationally representative, while its supplement documents quota-panel deviations: women 62.1% vs 51.3% population, tertiary-or-higher education 51.5% vs 37.0%, and AMBA 61.7% vs 45.0%.

design_structure.description: Eight randomized posts from the factorial combination of two candidates, two inflation-control claim contents, and two frame types.
Candidate can versus cannot control inflation.

study.preregistration_note: The supplementary file documents OSF preregistration on 2023-11-18 before field completion and notes a preregistration-abstract typo that gave November 2022 instead of the correct November 2023 field date.

effects.outcome: aggregate engagement main confirmation among counter-attitudinal

model_match: The current CBD uses the positive confirmation-by-congruence interaction and near-zero counter-attitudinal confirmation main effect as the differential target that distinguishes frame×congruence from frame-only.
limitations: The published interaction is defined using partisan congruence with 2023 runoff vote choice. M1 generalizes this only to a task-specific message–prior-attitude congruence relation and does not create a stable ideology or party-identity trait. The supplement documents multiple analysis bases (2075 achieved panel, 2074 consent/screening, 2044 treatment-distribution, 1901 complete-case regression) and notable composition deviations despite population-calibrated quotas; those bases must not be collapsed into a single unqualified N.

study.count_note: Main Results text reports 53,699 headlines in the filtered confirmatory sample; two figure captions report 53,669. CBD records the main-text count and preserves this 30-headline publication discrepancy as provenance context.
study.randomization_integrity_note: The Upworthy tests were designed as randomized A/B experiments, but the 2024 archive correction identifies 7,004 tests (22% of the archive) as potentially affected by a caching-related randomization problem and recommends omitting experiments from 2013-06-25 through 2014-01-10 for causal analyses. Archive maintainers report the Robertson findings were nearly identical when re-run on tests judged reliable.

effects.comparison: standardized proportion of negative words in otherwise comparable same-story headline experiments
effects.scale_note: Published standardized coefficient with 99% confidence interval; variables were z-standardized in the source analysis.

effects.comparison: one additional negative word in a headline of average length
effects.scale_note: Approximate source-reported CTR increase for a headline of average length; not a CBD coefficient.

model_match: The current CBD uses only the directional higher-Hneg to higher-Paccess pattern. The CBD binary Hneg cue and demonstrative logistic coefficient are not fitted to the source study's continuous standardized predictor or reported magnitude.
limitations: The primary causal evidence comes from historical Upworthy field experiments. The 2024 archive correction identifies 7,004 A/B tests (22% of the archive) as potentially affected and recommends excluding 2013-06-25 through 2014-01-10 for causal analyses; archive maintainers separately report the Robertson findings were nearly identical on tests judged reliable. Recent preprint-level experimental counterevidence from a different attention-economy task did not recover the expected negativity advantage, so CBD treats the direction as a bounded candidate rather than a universal constant.
